headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors; prompt-injection and leakage are lower due to limited shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads files and uses shared skill/context files, while agent B is a chat bot framework with multiple external channels. No direct shared channel is documented, so a prompt-injection bridge is possible only if outputs are manually copied or wired through files. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF operator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or bot training data, injection risk becomes active.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or message queue, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep a manual review step before any A output reaches B.
Strip instructions from A outputs before reuse.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
Disable any file-based handoff between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches marketing content and product marketing context, and agent B handles text and voice. Both have allowlisted egress, but no shared workspace, secrets, or sensitive regulated data are documented. Leakage is therefore possible only through operator-mediated transfer or an undocumented integration, so the blast radius appears small.
conditions: IF the operator places confidential customer or internal marketing data into both agents, leakage risk increases.
IF a shared filesystem or ticketing export is added, data can flow from A to B.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in either agent.
Use separate storage locations for each agent.
Review outbound destinations on both allowlists.
Redact sensitive fields before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can read and write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent B is a multi-instance-disabled bot framework with external API channels. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or bot assets, concurrent writes and state corruption are plausible. Because A's write surface is explicit and B's mutable surfaces are not fully specified, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or bot configuration, file clobbering can occur.
IF B is deployed with shared mutable state and A edits it concurrently, race conditions become active.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to A and B.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Run A in a read-only mode when possible.
Back up shared state before any joint run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces marketing content and context, and agent B is a dialogue system that can render or act on text. If B consumes A's output without verification, A's mistakes can cascade into customer-facing responses. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice over low.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated copy as authoritative response text, errors propagate to customers.
IF A's marketing claims are inserted into B's dialogue policy without review, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification checklist for claims and dates.
Limit B to templated responses when fed by A.
Log provenance for any A-to-B handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic text/voice or marketing data classes, with no PHI, EU PII, or residency mismatch stated. The compliance pathway is therefore limited to policy mismatch or undocumented deployment choices, not an inherent pairwise violation. No separate citation for the other agent is needed beyond the documented data classes and open-source status.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF deployment regions differ from data residency requirements, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Review vendor terms for each integration.
